basic.title: Basic Level
basic.description: Conditional Statements – if, if-else, elif, nested if

questions.question: Using nested if, accept application registration and approval status and determine whether API access can be granted.

questions.scenario: An HR application needs to display an employee's name, department, and salary.
questions.question: Define a function employee_details(name, department, salary) that accepts three positional arguments and displays the employee details.

questions.scenario: A construction application needs to calculate the area of a rectangular room using its length and width.
questions.question: Define a function calculate_area(length, width) that accepts two positional arguments and returns the area.

questions.scenario: A school wants to calculate a student's total marks in three subjects.
questions.question: Define a function total_marks(subject1, subject2, subject3) that accepts three positional arguments and returns their total.

questions.scenario: An online store needs to display product information such as product name, price, and brand.
questions.question: Define a function product_details(name, price, brand) and call it using keyword arguments.

questions.scenario: A movie application needs to display movie name, director, and release year.
questions.question: Define a function movie_details(name, director, year) and call it using keyword arguments in a different order.

questions.scenario: A delivery application needs to store a customer's name, city, and postal code.
questions.question: Define a function customer_address(name, city, pincode) and call it using keyword arguments.

questions.scenario: A mobile application processes recharges using a mobile number, recharge amount, and validity period.
questions.question: Define a function mobile_recharge(number, amount, validity) and call it by passing the mobile number as a positional argument and the remaining arguments as keyword arguments.

questions.scenario: A library maintains book records using book title, author, and publication year.
questions.question: Define a function book_details(title, author, year) and call it using a combination of positional and keyword arguments.

questions.scenario: An airline application needs passenger name, destination, and ticket class to create a booking summary.
questions.question: Define a function flight_booking(name, destination, ticket_class) and call it using a positional argument for the passenger name and keyword arguments for the remaining details.

questions.scenario: A weather application converts temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit.
questions.question: Define a function convert_temperature(celsius, /) that accepts only a positional argument and returns the Fahrenheit temperature. (Hint: use / in the function definition.)

questions.scenario: A mathematical application needs to calculate the square of a given number.
questions.question: Define a function calculate_square(number, /) that accepts only a positional argument and returns its square.

questions.scenario: A shopping application calculates a discount amount based on the original price and discount percentage.
questions.question: Define a function calculate_discount(price, percentage, /) that accepts two positional-only arguments and returns the discount amount.

questions.scenario: An application sends email notifications using the recipient's email address and message.
questions.question: Define a function send_email(*, email, message) that accepts only keyword arguments and displays the email details.

questions.scenario: A hotel booking system needs the number of guests and number of nights to calculate the total stay duration.
questions.question: Define a function hotel_booking(*, guests, nights) that accepts keyword-only arguments and displays the booking details.

questions.scenario: An online store calculates the final product price using its base price and tax percentage.
questions.question: Define a function final_price(*, price, tax) that accepts keyword-only arguments and returns the price after adding tax.

questions.scenario: A company calculates an employee's final salary using basic salary and bonus percentage.
questions.question: Define a function salary_calculation(basic_salary, /, *, bonus) where basic_salary is positional-only and bonus is keyword-only. Return the final salary.

questions.scenario: A travel application converts kilometres into miles using a conversion factor.
questions.question: Define a function convert_distance(kilometers, /, *, conversion_factor) where kilometres must be positional-only and conversion_factor must be keyword-only.

questions.scenario: An examination system calculates a student's result using total marks and maximum marks.
questions.question: Define a function student_result(total_marks, /, *, maximum_marks) where total_marks is positional-only and maximum_marks is keyword-only. Calculate and return the percentage.

questions.scenario: An online shopping application allows customers to purchase any number of products. The application needs to calculate the total price of all products.
questions.question: Define a function cart_total(*prices) that accepts multiple product prices and returns their total.

questions.scenario: A teacher wants to calculate the average marks of a student across multiple subjects. The number of subjects may vary.
questions.question: Define a function calculate_average(*marks) that accepts multiple marks and returns their average.

questions.scenario: A restaurant customer orders multiple food items. The billing system needs to calculate the total bill.
questions.question: Define a function restaurant_bill(*items) that accepts multiple item prices and returns the total bill.

questions.scenario: A mathematical application receives multiple numbers from a user and needs to identify the largest number.
questions.question: Define a function find_maximum(*numbers) that accepts any number of positional arguments and returns the largest number.

questions.scenario: A social media application stores different user details such as name, age, city, email, and profession. Different users may have different profile information.
questions.question: Define a function user_profile(**details) that accepts any number of keyword arguments and displays all the user information.

questions.scenario: An inventory application stores product details such as name, price, brand, category, and quantity. Additional product details may also be provided.
questions.question: Define a function register_product(**product_info) that accepts multiple keyword arguments and displays all product information.

questions.scenario: An HR system stores employee information such as employee ID, name, department, salary, and experience. The number of details may vary.
questions.question: Define a function employee_record(**details) that accepts variable-length keyword arguments and displays the employee record.

questions.scenario: A mobile application greets users. If the user does not provide a name, the application should display a default greeting using the name Guest.
questions.question: Define a function greet_user(name='Guest') that displays a greeting. Call it once without an argument and once with a name.

questions.scenario: A cinema application sells movie tickets. The default ticket price is ₹150, but users may choose a different ticket price.
questions.question: Define a function book_ticket(price=150) that displays the ticket price. Call it with and without an argument.

questions.scenario: An online store charges ₹50 as the default shipping fee. Some special delivery services may have a different shipping charge.
questions.question: Define a function shipping_cost(amount, delivery_charge=50) that adds the delivery charge to the order amount and returns the total.

questions.scenario: A company stores employee information. If the employee's department is not provided, the system should assign the default department as General.
questions.question: Define a function employee_info(name, department='General') that displays employee details. Call it with and without the department argument.

questions.scenario: A telecom application offers a default data recharge of 1 GB. Customers can select a different data amount when needed.
questions.question: Define a function data_recharge(data=1) that displays the selected data amount. Call it with and without an argument.

questions.scenario: A web application displays a welcome banner before showing user details.
questions.question: Create a decorator that displays 'Welcome to RaidenHub!' before executing a function that displays the user's name.

questions.scenario: A website wants to show a farewell message after displaying page content.
questions.question: Create a decorator that displays 'Thank you for visiting!' after a function displays a website's details.

questions.scenario: A monitoring system tracks when functions start and finish execution.
questions.question: Create a decorator that displays 'Function execution started' before calling a function and 'Function execution completed' after it finishes.

questions.scenario: A company wants to brand all its services with a common tagline.
questions.question: Create a decorator that displays 'Powered by RaidenHub TechStudio' before displaying a company's service details.

questions.scenario: A document editing application reminds users to save their work before viewing content.
questions.question: Create a decorator that displays 'Don't forget to save your work!' before executing a function that displays a document's content.

questions.scenario: A dashboard application restricts access to logged-in users only.
questions.question: Create a decorator that checks whether a user is logged in before allowing them to access a dashboard function.

questions.scenario: A website needs age verification before granting access to restricted content.
questions.question: Create a decorator that checks whether a customer's age is 18 or above before allowing them to access a restricted-content function.

questions.scenario: A bank requires a minimum account balance of ₹1,000 before any transaction.
questions.question: Create a decorator that checks whether a bank account has a minimum balance of ₹1,000 before allowing a transaction function to execute.

questions.scenario: An admin panel allows only admin users to delete records.
questions.question: Create a decorator that allows only users with the 'admin' role to execute a delete-record function.

questions.scenario: A calculator application needs to validate that inputs are positive before processing.
questions.question: Create a decorator that checks whether the number passed to a function is positive before calculating its square.

questions.scenario: An analytics system needs to track how many times each function is called.
questions.question: Create a decorator that counts how many times a function has been executed.

questions.scenario: A report generation system logs the start and end time of report creation.
questions.question: Create a decorator that displays start and end time messages whenever a report-generation function is executed.

questions.scenario: A division function needs protection against dividing by zero.
questions.question: Create a decorator that handles ZeroDivisionError when a function performs division.

questions.scenario: A registration form needs to validate that input fields are not empty.
questions.question: Create a decorator that checks whether the input provided to a customer-registration function is empty or not.

questions.scenario: A content system needs all output text in uppercase format.
questions.question: Create a decorator that converts the returned string from a function into uppercase.

questions.scenario: An e-commerce platform applies automatic discounts on product prices.
questions.question: Create a decorator that applies a 10% discount to the price returned by a product-price function.

questions.scenario: A security system logs which user accesses their profile.
questions.question: Create a decorator that displays the username whenever a user accesses a profile function.

questions.scenario: A calculator application needs formatted output for all results.
questions.question: Create a decorator that adds 'Result: ' before the value returned by a calculation function.

questions.scenario: A dashboard requires both authentication and a welcome message before access.

questions.scenario: A data processing pipeline needs to filter only float values from a mixed-type list.

questions.scenario: A mathematical utility needs to produce prime numbers on demand.

questions.question: Write a generator function that yields the square of each number from 1 to n.

advanced.title: Advanced Level
advanced.description: OOP, Exception Handling, Comprehensions, Lambda, Map, File Handling

questions.scenario: A school wants to store each student's name, age, roll number, and marks, and calculate the total and average marks.
questions.question: Create a Student class that uses a constructor, keeps name, age, roll_no, and marks as private attributes, stores marks in a list, has instance methods calculate_total() and calculate_average(), calculates the total with a loop, uses >, <, and == to check marks, and then creates two student objects and displays their details.

questions.scenario: A bank wants a simple system to manage customer accounts. Customers can deposit and withdraw money, and the balance must not be changed directly from outside the class.
questions.question: Create a BankAccount class with private __account_number, __name, and __balance attributes, a constructor, instance methods deposit() and withdraw(), and a check that rejects withdrawals greater than the balance. Store transactions in a list and display them with a loop.

questions.scenario: The BankAccount system needs a way to validate deposit amounts before processing.
questions.question: Add a @staticmethod to the BankAccount class that checks whether a deposit amount is valid.

questions.scenario: The bank wants to quickly create accounts from formatted strings like '101-Ravi-5000'.
questions.question: Add a @classmethod to the BankAccount class that creates an account from a string such as '101-Ravi-5000'.

questions.scenario: A company wants to store employee information and calculate salaries.
questions.question: Create an Employee class with private __name, __employee_id, and __salary attributes, a constructor, instance methods display_details() and increase_salary(), a @staticmethod that checks whether a salary is valid, and a @classmethod that creates an employee from a dictionary. Store multiple employees in a dictionary, display all of them with a loop, and find the employee with the highest salary.

questions.scenario: A rental company rents cars and bikes to customers. Vehicle → Car, Vehicle → Bike.
questions.question: Create Vehicle, Car, and Bike classes. Vehicle should have private __vehicle_number, __model, and __price_per_day attributes. Car and Bike inherit from Vehicle and override calculate_rent(). Add a static method to check valid rental days. Store rented vehicles in a list and find vehicles costing more than ₹1,000 per day.

questions.scenario: A library wants to maintain books that can be borrowed and returned.
questions.question: Create a Book class with private __title, __author, __price, and __available attributes. Add borrow_book(), return_book(), display_book(). Store books in a list. Add a static method to validate price, a class method to create from 'Python Basics-Ravi-500'. Use == to compare titles.

questions.scenario: An online shopping website lets customers add products to a cart.
questions.question: Create Product and ShoppingCart classes. Product has private __name, __price, __quantity. Add/remove products, calculate total with a loop. Add a static method for price validation, class method from dictionary, @discount decorator for 10% off.

questions.scenario: A mobile phone has a brand, model, battery percentage, and installed applications.
questions.question: Create a MobilePhone class with private __brand, __model, __battery, __apps. Add install_app(), remove_app(), charge_phone(). Store apps in a list. Add static method for battery validation, class method from dictionary, decorator that prints 'Phone operation started'.

questions.scenario: A small shop wants to track its products and stock.
questions.question: Create a Product class with private __product_id, __name, __price, __stock. Add add_stock() and sell_product(). Prevent selling when stock is insufficient. Store products in a dictionary, categories in a set. Add static method for stock validation, class method from dictionary, decorator that prints 'Stock updated'.
